name: tmux Sessions
description: Lets Claude manage tmux sessions on Linux — start long-running jobs, check their output, send keystrokes, and kill them.
long_description:
Designed for long-running ML training, data pipelines, and other jobs you want to survive beyond a single Claude conversation. Claude can start a detached tmux session with an initial command, capture the last N lines of a pane to check progress, send keys (including Ctrl+C), and terminate sessions.

**Typical workflow:** start a training run inside a named session, have Claude check its progress an hour later by capturing the pane, and either let it continue, interrupt it, or kill the session entirely. You can also `tmux attach -t <name>` from any terminal to watch the job live — Claude and a human can observe the same session simultaneously.

**Requires** `tmux` installed on the system (`sudo apt install tmux`). No npm dependencies.

**Scope:** tmux only in v0.1. No window/pane splitting, no `tmux attach` (that's done from a real terminal, not via MCP). systemd --user service control may land in a later version.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: List all tmux sessions on the current user's tmux server. Returns name, window count, created/activity timestamps, and attached status. Returns an empty list if no tmux server is running.

tools.name: has_session
tools.description: Check whether a named tmux session exists. Cheap precondition for capture_pane / send_keys.

tools.name: list_windows
tools.description: List windows within a named session (index, name, active flag, pane count).

tools.name: capture_pane
tools.description: Capture the last N lines of text visible in a session's active pane (default 100). The primitive for 'is my training still running?'.

tools.name: new_session
tools.description: Start a new detached tmux session with a given name. Optionally runs an initial command inside the shell (sent as keystrokes + Enter, so shell features like aliases and venvs work as expected).

tools.name: send_keys
tools.description: Send key combos or text to a session's active pane. Useful for C-c (interrupt), C-d (close), or typing a command. Text is sent literally; combos use tmux key notation.

tools.name: kill_session
tools.description: Terminate a named tmux session. Any processes running inside (including the initial command) are sent SIGHUP.
